scope: Defence and security procurement and industry at Union level: DAC approvals and MoD contracts as PIB names them (an `award` claim only where PIB names the vendor and the ₹ crore; joint totals, AoNs and unpriced contracts are facts on the buyer with the void 'vendor not named' or 'amount not stated'); DPSU and private production, exports and licences by year from the DDP tables and PIB; the licensed private producers (L&T, Bharat Forge, Solar Industries/EEL, Mahindra, Tata Advanced Systems, Adani Defence and PLR Systems, Data Patterns, Zen, Astra, Paras, MTAR) and Reliance Naval's NCLT outcome; offsets, the Dassault-Reliance JV and the 2016 Rafale contract; the two defence corridors and iDEX; SIPRI import shares. Three levels of resolution: Union money resolves to the line item; state money resolves to the Police major head per state (and prisons per state from NCRB), with strength and per-capita figures `reported:` while BPR&D is down; city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (installations, commissionerate entities with `reported:` strength) and the void. This file touches only the Union procurement and industry level; it carries no state or city money. It leaves out unannounced procurement, deployments and orders of battle, and carries no budget or strength series.

Value: Reuters on the signing day: 'close to 7.8 billion euros ($8.7 billion)' and '$1 = 0.8920 euros' — Reuters converted to dollars, not rupees; 'India's defence ministry said it would confirm the exact price later' [documented]. The € 7.87 billion / ~₹59,000 crore pair is the figure press and Dassault quote; no opened primary record states a ₹/€ rate; the pair implies ≈ ₹74.96 per euro [analytic]. CAG Report No. 3 of 2019, Part B: the contract at “U” million € was '2.86 per cent lower than Audit's aligned price'; a Letter of Comfort signed by the French Prime Minister replaced bank guarantees; 'Offset contract with 50 per cent value of (a) and (b) above excluding the PBL and STAAM costs' (Part B para 1(c)); the report names neither Reliance nor DRAL [documented]

PIB 2019-11-20: the Government told Lok Sabha that CAG found the package price 2.86% lower than the audit-aligned price and that 'Indian Government has not recommended any company for making Rafale jets for India' [documented]

narratives.strongestCase: Adani Enterprises has built a defence business (ADSTL / Adani Defence & Aerospace) quickly: a 51% holding in PLR Systems (reported), a 500-acre ammunition complex at Kanpur inside the UP Defence Industrial Corridor, a Hyderabad UAV and missile complex, an 85.8% purchase of Air Works (enterprise value ₹400 crore, announced 2024-12-23), and the only PIB-named award in this file to an Adani-linked vendor — the 2025-12-30 CQB carbine contract (₹2,770 crore for Bharat Forge and PLR Systems together; over 4.25 lakh carbines). A Gwalior small-arms maker winning part of a first-of-its-kind carbine buy, in a group that already holds ports, airports and power, is the visible core of the narrative. narratives.claim: Make in India has not reduced imports.
narratives.strongestCase: India was still the world's second-largest arms importer in both SIPRI periods (8.3% of the world total in 2020-24, 8.2% in 2021-25), its imports fell only 9.3% then 4.0% in volume, SIPRI says its 'recent orders or planned orders — including up to 140 combat aircraft from France and 6 submarines from Germany — indicate its continued and probably increasing reliance on foreign suppliers', the 26 Rafale-Marine IGA (2025-04-28), a Rafale MRFA AoN (2026-02-12), a P-8I AoN and a US$ MQ-9B deal all sit in the pipeline, and flagship 'indigenous' aircraft carry foreign engines (113 GE F404 for the 97 LCA Mk1A; AL-31FP made under licence from the Russian OEM).

PIB-named MoD award value 2021-25 (sample of PIB-named releases; joint contracts counted once): DPSUs 77.2% (HAL 58.1%), private Indian vendors 8.7% (L&T ₹24,984.65 crore sole-vendor, 6.1%; Bharat Forge/TASL ₹6,900 crore joint, 1.7%; Bharat Forge/PLR (Adani Defence 51%) ₹2,770 crore joint, 0.68%), the BrahMos JV 5.5%, foreign vendors 5.4%, other PSU 0.7%, a Pinaka EEL/MIL mixed contract 2.5%. The identical lens run on DPSUs and on the private vendors returns the same pattern — a few mega-contracts to the platform designer dominate — which is a finding about the lens (concentration by platform design), not about any vendor. Where a DPSU and a private vendor sit on one contract (Pinaka: EEL beside Munitions India) or one category (radars: L&T beside BEL; vessels: L&T and Chowgule beside Goa Shipyard/GRSE/Cochin/HSL; artillery: L&T, Bharat Forge, TASL beside the ordnance successors), the PIB gives joint totals and no bid counts, so no head-to-head can be scored. Union: UPA-II (FY2009-10 to 2013-14) versus NDA (FY2014-15 to 2025-26) on production, exports and imports: production ₹43,746 crore in 2013-14 against ₹46,429 crore (2014-15) to ₹1.78 lakh crore (2025-26); exports ₹686 crore (2013-14) to ₹38,424 crore; licences 215 (2014) to 788; SIPRI import share 9.1-9.3% (2015-20) to 8.2-8.3% (2020-25); the UPA-II end-year series for production and licences by year was not collected (gap), so growth rates across the two governments are only partly comparable.
